instructions: For each item in review_these: read the finding, then set review.accurate (true if it faithfully represents its source), review.keep (true if you would actually keep it -- the real kept-rate signal), and review.why_not (one short line, only when keep is false). Do not look at _scoring_key until you are done with every item -- it names the model and would un-blind the review. 40 items from the fixed 8-source E5 cohort, 5 importance-stratified findings per source.

review_these.title: Three broker questions generated by AI based on Kelly's methodology
review_these.content: AI identifies high-priority questions specific to each deal (e.g., broker identity, customer concentration, management structure) rather than generic inquiry templates. [1]

citations.title: AI found the business. AI helped finance it. I make $850k/yr
citations.snippet: Also identify three specific questions I should ask the broker during my first call because I've trained it with my specific criteria.

review_these.title: Tighter rules push amateur buyers out of the market
review_these.content: The added complexity discourages less-educated buyers, reducing competition and improving pricing and negotiation leverage for serious, well-structured buyers. [1]

citations.title: Everything You Need To Know About The Recent SBA Changes
citations.snippet: There are fewer amateur buyers now in the market. There's more room to negotiate on the price

review_these.title: No single customer should exceed 10% of revenue
review_these.content: Sellers rarely volunteer concentration data, so buyers must request a client-by-client revenue breakdown and treat any client over 10% as a major red flag, especially in $1-2M revenue businesses. [1]

citations.title: The 3 Most Important Factors When Buying A Business (MUST WATCH)
citations.snippet: if someone is more than that 10%, you have to really go into it

review_these.title: Deal Hunter prompt: sourcing criteria for ChatGPT
review_these.content: Feed ChatGPT revenue $500K–$5M, cash flow margin 15–35% ('golden ratio'), recession-resistant/recurring-revenue industries (HVAC, plumbing, accounting, waste management), and an existing GM/management team so you're not just buying a job. [1]

citations.title: AI found the business. AI helped finance it. I make $850k/yr
citations.snippet: revenue between 500,000 and 5 million. Two, cash flow margin between 15 and 35%

review_these.title: Example deal: $657K revenue, $422K cash flow, $500K ask
review_these.content: A Las Vegas landscaping business asking $500K on $657K revenue and $422K claimed SDE, used as the live case study for the teardown. [1]

citations.title: Live Deal Teardown: A $422K Cash-Flow Listing — Claimed, Supported, Missing - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: $657K revenue, $422K cash flow, $500K asking

review_these.title: Conservative cash-flow projections are mandatory
review_these.content: Always underestimate revenue and overestimate expenses; rosy projections typically fall short due to unforeseen costs and business disruptions, risking default on seller notes. [1]

citations.title: How To Buy A Business With Seller Financing (Step-By-Step)
citations.snippet: It is always better to be conservative when it comes to cash flow projections

review_these.title: Buyers must now bring 5% cash equity minimum
review_these.content: Previously buyers could reach 0% down using a seller note on full standby, but now the bank requires at least 5% from the buyer or an investor regardless of seller note structuring. [1]

citations.title: Everything You Need To Know About The Recent SBA Changes
citations.snippet: You now need to bring 5% of your own money or investors money to get a deal done

review_these.title: Key-man risk: 1-2 employees can hold all the leverage
review_these.content: If the business depends on one or two non-owner employees, they must be locked down contractually (equity, non-competes) or they can leave and take clients, since only the seller—not employees—typically signs a non-compete. [1]

citations.title: The 3 Most Important Factors When Buying A Business (MUST WATCH)
citations.snippet: That business relies on one to two essential people outside the seller

review_these.title: Screen industry for looming regulatory risk
review_these.content: Have legal counsel review pending legislation and current compliance status, since regulatory shifts can materially affect small-business profitability and buyers must ensure existing operations already follow the rules. [1]

citations.title: The 3 Most Important Factors When Buying A Business (MUST WATCH)
citations.snippet: regulatory changes that are happening through Congress...that could materially affect the industry

review_these.title: Check for post-close upside levers
review_these.content: A good acquisition requires identifiable opportunities to expand customers, add services, or pursue bolt-on acquisitions after closing — not just organic stability. [1]

citations.title: The Difference Between a Good Business and a Good Acquisition - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: Are there logical ways to expand the customer base, add new services, or pursue acquisitions?

review_these.title: Price must match growth assumptions and downside case
review_these.content: Buyers often get excited about business quality and forget to check whether entry price, growth assumptions, and downside scenario align. [1]

citations.title: The Difference Between a Good Business and a Good Acquisition - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: forget to ask whether the entry price, growth assumptions, and downside case make sense together

review_these.title: Verify SDE/EBITDA and scrutinize add-backs
review_these.content: Common junk add-backs include owner salary with no manager in place, one-time marketing that recurs, and personal expenses (travel, meals, car leases) the business actually needs to operate; if unverifiable, assume they're false. [1]

citations.title: 5-Minute CIM Review for Busy Business Buyers
citations.snippet: If it says 500K in cash flow, ask is that SDE or is that EBIDA? Then are the adbacks real or legitimate or are they just puffed up?

review_these.title: Seller note on full standby can satisfy injection, enabling 5% down
review_these.content: A seller note of 10%+ held on full standby for the life of a typically 10-year loan counts toward the buyer's required injection, dropping cash-down needs. [1]

citations.title: AI found the business. AI helped finance it. I make $850k/yr
citations.snippet: Seller notes of 10% plus on full standby for the life of the loan... can count as buyer injection, enabling down to a 5% down payment rule

review_these.title: Deferred equipment maintenance inflates apparent profit
review_these.content: Sellers may skip essential maintenance to boost margins, leaving buyers to inherit broken equipment requiring costly near-term replacement — get a third-party equipment appraisal to check remaining life. [1]

citations.title: The 3 Most Important Factors When Buying A Business (MUST WATCH)
citations.snippet: sellers in order to show more profit margin will forego doing that essential maintenance

review_these.title: Other seller alternatives: consulting deals, bonuses, earnouts
review_these.content: Instead of granting ownership equity, buyers can use consulting agreements, performance-based bonuses, profit sharing without equity, and creative earnout structures to keep sellers incentivized without co-borrower risk. [1]

citations.title: Everything You Need To Know About The Recent SBA Changes
citations.snippet: Higher purchase price with long-term seller consulting, performance bonuses instead of equity, phantom equity arrangements

review_these.title: Deferred equipment maintenance inflates apparent profit
review_these.content: Sellers may skip essential maintenance to boost margins, leaving buyers to inherit broken equipment requiring costly near-term replacement — get a third-party equipment appraisal to check remaining life. [1]

citations.title: The 3 Most Important Factors When Buying A Business (MUST WATCH)
citations.snippet: sellers in order to show more profit margin will forego doing that essential maintenance

review_these.title: Check whether price/SDE and price/revenue multiples agree
review_these.content: The listing prices at 1.18x cash flow (below bottom-quartile comps) but 0.76x revenue (right at category average) — when a listing's own two multiples disagree, one of them is signaling something is off with the underlying numbers. [1]

citations.title: Live Deal Teardown: A $422K Cash-Flow Listing — Claimed, Supported, Missing - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: The listing's own two multiples disagree with each other. One of them is telling you something.

review_these.title: Capital stack affects business resilience
review_these.content: A debt-free business is considered more resilient than one burdened with debt and preferred equity hurdles, a factor relevant to financing structure decisions. [1]

citations.title: The Difference Between a Good Business and a Good Acquisition - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: An established business running without debt will be more 'resilient' than one with a debt

review_these.title: 64% margin vs 26.5% category median is a red flag
review_these.content: A listing claiming $422K cash flow on $657K revenue implies a 64% margin, more than double the sold-business median of 26.5% for that category per BizBuySell data (n=945), meaning it needs corroborating documentation, not automatic rejection. [1]

citations.title: Live Deal Teardown: A $422K Cash-Flow Listing — Claimed, Supported, Missing - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: BizBuySell's sold data for this category (n=945) puts the median at 26.5%

review_these.title: Reject deals without three years of P&Ls and balance sheets
review_these.content: If a SIM lacks at least three years of P&Ls and current balance sheet, request tax returns, QuickBooks files, cash flow statements, and bank statements; if the broker stalls or can't produce them, walk immediately. [1]

citations.title: 5-Minute CIM Review for Busy Business Buyers
citations.snippet: If the SIM doesn't include at least three years of P&Ls and a current balance sheet, you should stop on this one. No numbers, no deal.

review_these.title: Deal Structure prompt generates three financing scenarios instantly
review_these.content: Maximum SBA leverage (90% SBA + 10% seller note standby), traditional structure (90% SBA + 10% cash), and creative structure (90% SBA + 10% private investor equity) with cash requirements and monthly debt service at 8-10% SBA rates. [1]

citations.title: AI found the business. AI helped finance it. I make $850k/yr
citations.snippet: Create three financing structures. One, maximum SBA leverage, 90% SBA loan, 10% seller note on full standby.

review_these.title: Seller financing needs no personal credit check or guarantee
review_these.content: Unlike SBA loans, seller-financed deals typically skip personal credit checks and are often structured without a personal guarantee, though this is negotiable deal-by-deal. [1]

citations.title: How To Buy A Business With Seller Financing (Step-By-Step)
citations.snippet: there's not going to be any personal credit check required

review_these.title: Ignore broker urgency pressure and hype tactics
review_these.content: Brokers claiming 'four LOIs on this' or 'move fast' are using artificial scarcity; ignore it and instead ask yourself if it's actually a good business with verified financials. [1]

citations.title: 5-Minute CIM Review for Busy Business Buyers
citations.snippet: They'll tell you, 'Hey, we've got four LOIs on this. You need to move fast.' Ignore that hype. Ask yourself, is this actually a good business?

review_these.title: Owner works 30 hrs but business runs 45
review_these.content: Operating hours are 7am-4pm Mon-Fri (45 hrs/week) while the owner claims only 30 owner-hours, meaning someone else covers roughly 15 hours — a staffing/dependency question for diligence. [1]

citations.title: Live Deal Teardown: A $422K Cash-Flow Listing — Claimed, Supported, Missing - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: Operating hours are 7–4, Mon–Fri. The owner's stated hours are 30 a week

review_these.title: SBA rules have changed four times during Kelly's career
review_these.content: He frames each rule change historically as sparking temporary panic but notes deal-makers consistently adapt and continue closing deals. [1]

citations.title: Everything You Need To Know About The Recent SBA Changes
citations.snippet: The SBA has changed the rules four times since I got into acquisitions

review_these.title: Plan acquisition criteria in single focused session
review_these.content: Map out ideal business types and industries in a few hours over a weekend to gain clarity and prepare to recognize and act on perfect deals quickly. [1]

citations.title: Recession-Proof Portfolio Builder.pdf
citations.snippet: Spend a few hours on a weekend mapping out what types of businesses fit your criteria. You'll be poised to take advantage.

review_these.title: Verify why the seller's revenue exists relative to market size
review_these.content: Buyers should confirm the served market is much larger than the seller's current revenue/profit, and understand specifically why this small seller is capturing that revenue before assuming demand is durable. [1]

citations.title: The Difference Between a Good Business and a Good Acquisition - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: Buyer understands why this small seller is getting revenue and profit

review_these.title: Listing's two valuation multiples contradict each other
review_these.content: Priced at 1.18x cash flow (below bottom quartile for the category) but 0.76x revenue (right at category average), meaning one of the two multiples is signaling something is off about the true earnings. [1]

citations.title: Live Deal Teardown: A $422K Cash-Flow Listing — Claimed, Supported, Missing - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: The listing's own two multiples disagree with each other. One of them is telling you something.

review_these.title: Build defensible competitive moat before buying
review_these.content: Strong moats include licensing, complex logistics, deep relationships, contracts, or niche reputation; commoditized price-based competition should be avoided. [1]

citations.title: Recession-Proof Portfolio Builder.pdf
citations.snippet: The day after you buy it, no one should be able to easily copy it. Strong moats include licensing, certifications, deep relationships.

review_these.title: Document seller roles and responsibilities in writing
review_these.content: Spell out in the purchase agreement exactly what the seller will do during transition (introductions to key relationships, training, documentation) rather than relying on verbal promises. [1]

citations.title: How To Buy A Business With Seller Financing (Step-By-Step)
citations.snippet: making sure that the seller involvement is in writing in the contract. You never trust that the seller is going to stay around

review_these.title: Identify key man risk and operational dependencies
review_these.content: If the owner is doing everything or one technician holds all knowledge, you inherit a critical point of failure that requires immediate remediation post-close. [1]

citations.title: 5-Minute CIM Review for Busy Business Buyers
citations.snippet: Is there a GM or is the owner doing everything? Any key man risk. If the seller is the glue and they're leaving, you've got a lot of work to do.

review_these.title: Seller-retained equity now triggers personal guarantee requirement
review_these.content: If a seller keeps equity (partial buyout or rolled-equity deal), they and all other equity holders/investors must become co-borrowers on the buyer's SBA loan, which most sellers/investors won't accept. [1]

citations.title: Everything You Need To Know About The Recent SBA Changes
citations.snippet: If the seller maintains equity in the deal, they will now have to personally guarantee the buyer's loan

review_these.title: Seller financing avoids personal credit checks entirely
review_these.content: Unlike bank loans, seller financing deals don't require a credit check because the seller is betting on the business's cash flow and the buyer's ability to run it, not on traditional creditworthiness metrics. [1]

citations.title: How To Buy A Business With Seller Financing (Step-By-Step)
citations.snippet: one of the biggest benefits is there's not going to be any personal credit check required

review_these.title: Starting offer 15-20% below fair market value range
review_these.content: Kelly's methodology caps maximum offer price at this discount to fair value, with AI applying this rule consistently across deal analysis. [1]

citations.title: AI found the business. AI helped finance it. I make $850k/yr
citations.snippet: I typically start 15 to 20% below fair value.

review_these.title: Accounting, bookkeeping, and pet services recession-proof
review_these.content: These sectors have sticky recurring customers and non-discretionary demand; people maintain business records and pet care regardless of economic conditions. [1]

citations.title: Recession-Proof Portfolio Builder.pdf
citations.snippet: Accounting / Bookkeeping Required every year. Pet Services People cut back on themselves before their pets.

review_these.title: Fax Machine Factor: target businesses stuck in time
review_these.content: Look for paper files, no CRM, cash-only operations, or no website — these can be modernized with simple systems within 90 days for near-immediate cash flow gains, directly matching the user's stated interest in AI/automation upside. [1]

citations.title: Recession-Proof Portfolio Builder.pdf
citations.snippet: Seek businesses that are “stuck in time”—and still making money.

review_these.title: Five red flags to screen out immediately
review_these.content: Reject project-based/long sales cycle businesses, single-client/vendor dependency, hyper-regulated industries you don't understand, trend-chasing fads, and owner-operated businesses lacking a team or systems. [1]

citations.title: Recession-Proof Portfolio Builder.pdf
citations.snippet: Owner-operated businesses with no team or systems in place

review_these.title: Spend $2–5K on CPA/attorney to prevent $100K mistakes
review_these.content: Professional financial and legal review on deals that pass the filter is far cheaper insurance than missing fatal flaws or overpaying. [1]

citations.title: 5-Minute CIM Review for Busy Business Buyers
citations.snippet: Bring in a CPA or an M&A attorney if it's a real deal. A few thousand bucks to avoid 100k mistake. Totally worth it.

review_these.title: A bad business at a low price is still a bad acquisition
review_these.content: Low purchase price does not rescue a fundamentally weak business — price only affects ROI on an already-good business, not whether a bad one becomes investable. [1]

citations.title: The Difference Between a Good Business and a Good Acquisition - Searchfunder
citations.snippet: A bad business at low price is a bad acquisition

review_these.title: Weekly standing meeting prevents buyer-seller breakdown
review_these.content: A recurring check-in (e.g., a Wednesday lunch or Zoom call) is recommended to maintain communication and avoid resentment during the post-sale transition when the seller is still owed payments. [1]

citations.title: How To Buy A Business With Seller Financing (Step-By-Step)
citations.snippet: you have a standing meeting every Wednesday at noon where you have lunch together
